Repair under AR-F01: read confinement and resource bounds. recovery.open_confined validates the recorded path text then os.lstat-checks every component (symlink and resolved-escape rejection), requires a regular file, opens with O_RDONLY|O_NOFOLLOW and re-checks os.fstat device/inode before any read; read_confined_bytes reads at most the caller bound + 1 and never parses partial bytes; recover_stream streams line-by-line under max_event_bytes and the derived max_events*max_event_bytes total with max_read_records capping and max_diagnostic_count capping; the manifest read is bounded by max_manifest_bytes. Caller limits stay authoritative and the manifest limits echo is combined by per-field minimum.

Repair under AR-F02: EvidenceReader exposes recorded_evidence_status/reasons (manifest facts, verbatim) separately from assessed_evidence_status/reasons (reader conclusion); export_json carries the assessed status as the primary evidenceStatus with the recorded facts alongside; the CLI exits 0 only on assessed complete and never presents primary complete for corrupt evidence.

Repair under AR-F03: validate_event_record re-applies the complete closed event/clock/observation/snapshot schema on read and requires runId/eventId/producerId, positive ingestionOrdinal, declared clock units/domains and finite values; the recovery loop enforces per-run eventId uniqueness, strictly increasing ingestionOrdinal and manifest run-ID consistency. Malformed container/version/decode/bound/I/O faults become closed-catalogue diagnostics; no TypeError/ValueError/JSON error escapes the reader or CLI. Revision 4 closes the residual manifest-side gap: schema.find_nonfinite performs a bounded, iterative full scan of the parsed manifest and reader.read_run rejects any NaN/Infinity (including an overflowing 1e400 literal) anywhere in it with one stable ARGUS2-INPUT-NONFINITE diagnostic before the schema-version check, limits echo, assessment or export; the recorded manifest facts remain separately preserved and the run is assessed incomplete.

Repair under AR-F04: writer._publish is the single manifest publication chokepoint and measures the actual canonical serialized bytes against max_manifest_bytes before creating a temporary file; open, successful finalize, failed finalize and abort all route through it and the writer state advances to closed only after publication succeeds, so a bound or I/O failure preserves the prior manifest bytes and never claims closed/complete. Revision 4 bounds the exact bytes that would be written including the manifest's single trailing newline (len(encoded) + 1) in both _publish and the open_run preflight, so an over-bound open is refused before any run root is created.

Repair under AR-F05: api._admission_snapshot canonical-round-trips each admitted obligation (including nested detail); the run-envelope clock, source-byte digests, clocks, annotation and extensions are deep-copied at admission; record_artifact returns an independent copy while owning its size/hash identity internally; the reader and manifest accessors return defensive deep copies so post-admission caller mutation cannot lower an obligation or rewrite an indexed hash.

The C++ interoperability producer remains owned test material compiled under /tmp with g++ -std=c++20 against the accepted src/xverse/xcom headers and the accepted observation.cpp/item.cpp/contract.cpp/value.cpp/diagnostic.cpp translation units; no accepted C++/XDL source, schema, CLI or historical record was modified.

The wheel is built and installed offline (python -m build --no-isolation; pip install --no-deps --no-index --target) and the owned tests repeat outside the source tree with PYTHONPATH resolving only to the installed target; ARGUS_PLATFORM_SOURCE_ROOT resolves the accepted platform sources/fixtures, falling back to the repository root in ordinary local tests.
